06-12.act: Handle today's work well. Leave tomorrow to God.

06-13.prayer: Lord, keep me honest in business. No fudged numbers, no padded invoices, no half-truths to customers. Let my scales be accurate, because You're watching even when no one else is.
06-13.text: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.
06-13.reflect: Fudged numbers, padded hours, half-truths to customers. God sees all of it.
06-13.act: Correct one thing at work that isn't fully honest.

06-14.prayer: Jesus, You got up before dark to pray before the crowds came. Teach me to start my day like You did. Win the morning with You, then go to work.
06-14.text: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and slipped out to a solitary place to pray.
06-14.reflect: Jesus won the morning before the crowds came. How do your mornings start?
06-14.act: Build a morning routine: prayer, Scripture, movement. Then work.

06-15.prayer: God, give me good will toward the people I work for and with. Bosses, clients, customers, crew. Help me serve them like I'm serving You, even when they don't deserve it.
06-15.text: Serve with good will, as to the Lord and not to men.
06-15.reflect: Do you serve your boss, clients, or customers with good will or a bad attitude?
06-15.act: Serve someone at work today with a genuinely good attitude.

06-16.prayer: Lord, make me faithful in the small stuff. The small jobs, the small details, the small promises. That's where character gets built, and that's where You're watching.
06-16.text: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
06-16.reflect: Small compromises lead to big ones. Where are you cutting small corners?
06-16.act: Do one small job perfectly today, even if no one notices.

06-17.prayer: Father, my job is a tool, but You're my provider. Take the panic out of my finances and replace it with trust. Supply what we need, and help me be content with it.
06-17.text: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
06-17.reflect: Your job is a tool. God is the source. Do you trust the tool or the Source?
06-17.act: Pray about your finances today with trust, not panic.

06-18.prayer: Lord, I give You my first and best, not my leftovers. My first hour, my first dollars, my first energy. Help me honor You with what I have before I spend it on me.
06-18.text: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest; then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
06-18.reflect: Does God get your first or your leftovers?
06-18.act: Look at your budget. Make sure giving comes first.

06-19.prayer: Jesus, You led by serving. Make me a servant leader. Let the people under me feel served, not used, and let my leadership look more like a towel than a throne.
06-19.text: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant.
06-19.reflect: If you lead people, do they feel served or used?
06-19.act: Serve someone who works for or with you today in a way they don't expect.

06-20.prayer: God, help me pay attention to what You've put in my care: my finances, my team, my family, my health. Show me what I've been avoiding, and give me the courage to look.
06-20.text: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds.
06-20.reflect: Do you know the real state of your finances? Your team? Your family?
06-20.act: Check in on one thing you've been avoiding looking at.

06-21.prayer: Lord, sometimes You have to make me lie down. Lead me to green pastures and quiet waters. Get me off the screens and outside. Restore my soul and my body.
06-21.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters. He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.
06-21.reflect: Sometimes God has to make you lie down. When did you last unplug and get outside?
06-21.act: Get outside today. Walk, hike, or sit by water. No screens.

06-22.prayer: God, I've talked about some things for way too long. Help me do more than talk. Give me the discipline to take the first real step today.
06-22.text: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
06-22.reflect: What have you been talking about doing for too long?
06-22.act: Take the first real step on it today.

06-23.prayer: Lord, distractions keep calling me off the wall. Keep me focused on the work You gave me. Like Nehemiah, give me the backbone to say, "I'm doing a great work. I can't come down."
06-23.text: So I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to go down to you?”
06-23.reflect: Distractions will always call. What's pulling you off the wall?
06-23.act: Say no to one distraction today so you can finish what matters.

06-24.prayer: God, I make too many decisions in a hurry. Help me plan wisely. Slow me down long enough to pray, think, and get counsel before I act.
06-24.text: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.
06-24.reflect: Are you making rushed decisions at work or with money?
06-24.act: Slow down on one big decision. Pray and plan before you act.

06-25.prayer: Lord, my life is a mist, here and gone. All my plans are in Your hands. Help me hold them loosely and plan with You, not just around You.
06-25.text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.” You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes. Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
06-25.reflect: Do you plan with God or just around Him?
06-25.act: Add "if the Lord wills" to your plans today. Mean it.

06-26.prayer: God, help me build wealth the right way. Slow, honest, and steady. Keep me from shortcuts that dwindle, and help me be wise with every dollar You trust me with.
06-26.text: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.
06-26.reflect: Slow and honest beats fast and shady. Every time.
06-26.act: Put something toward savings today, even if it's small.

06-27.prayer: Lord, I have people who answer to me, and I answer to You. Help me treat them with fairness and respect. Let them see in how I lead that I have a Master in heaven.
06-27.text: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
06-27.reflect: If you're the boss, remember you have a Boss. How would He grade the way you lead?
06-27.act: Recognize someone on your team today. Be specific.

06-28.prayer: God, teach me to number my days. Work will always want more of me. Help me give my health, my family, and You the time they deserve while I still have it.
06-28.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.
06-28.reflect: Nobody on their deathbed wishes they'd worked more. Is your health getting your leftover time?
06-28.act: Block time on your calendar this week for exercise. Treat it like a client meeting.

06-29.prayer: Lord, rest is a gift, but laziness is a thief. Keep me from laziness. Give me the honesty to tell the difference in my own life, and the discipline to get up and go.
06-29.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest, and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
06-29.reflect: Rest is good. Laziness isn't. Do you know the difference in your own life?
06-29.act: Get up on time tomorrow. No snooze.

06-30.prayer: Lord, I don't need to be famous. I need to be faithful. More than any raise or award, I want to hear "well done."
06-30.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
06-30.reflect: Faithful, not famous. Would God say "well done" about your work this month?
06-30.act: Review your month. Thank God for the wins. Own the misses.

07-01.prayer: Lord, You commanded me to be strong and courageous, and You promised to go with me. Make me that man today. Show me where fear has been calling the shots, and give me the nerve to obey.
07-01.text: Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
07-01.reflect: Courage is a command, not a personality type. Where are you disobeying out of fear?
07-01.act: Do the thing you've been afraid to do. Today.

07-02.prayer: God, I'm not as strong as I act. Hold me up with Your right hand. Strengthen me, help me, and steady me for whatever today throws at me.
07-02.text: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My right hand of righteousness.
07-02.reflect: Five promises in one verse. Which one do you need most today?
07-02.act: Write that promise down and carry it with you.

07-03.prayer: Lord, fear didn't come from You. Drive it out. Replace it with power, love, and self-discipline. Let me face today with a clear head and a steady heart.
07-03.text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
07-03.reflect: Fear isn't from God. So where did it come from, and why are you listening to it?
07-03.act: Name your biggest fear out loud. Then pray this verse over it.

07-04.prayer: God, You will never leave me or forsake me. I'm counting on it. Thank You for the freedom I enjoy and the men who paid for it. Make me brave enough to live free.
07-04.text: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you.
07-04.reflect: Freedom costs courage. What freedom in your life is fear holding hostage?
07-04.act: Thank God for the freedom you have. Pray for those who fought for it.

07-05.prayer: Lord, You're my light, my salvation, and my stronghold. So who do I need to fear? Shrink the people and problems I've made too big, and put You back where You belong.
07-05.text: Of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation— whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life— whom shall I dread?
07-05.reflect: Make a list of who or what you fear. Hold it up next to God. Still scared?
07-05.act: Face one person you've been avoiding.

07-06.prayer: God, there's a giant in front of me. I'm not going out in my own strength. I come in Your name, like David did. Give me the faith to take the first step toward it.
07-06.text: But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.”
07-06.reflect: What giant is standing in front of you? Whose name are you facing it in?
07-06.act: Take one step toward your giant today.

07-07.prayer: Lord, David was ready for Goliath because he'd fought lions and bears when nobody was watching. Prepare me in the hidden places. Let my early workouts and quiet times build a man ready for battle.
07-07.text: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock, I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.”
07-07.reflect: David was ready for Goliath because he trained when nobody was watching. Your early-morning workouts count. So does your quiet time.
07-07.act: Train today like you're preparing for a battle you can't see yet.

07-08.prayer: God, maybe I'm here for such a time as this. Help me speak up when it matters, even if it costs me. Don't let me hide in silence when someone needs a voice.
07-08.text: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
07-08.reflect: Where are you staying silent when you should speak?
07-08.act: Say the thing that needs to be said. With love, but say it.

07-09.prayer: Lord, You're able to deliver me. But even if You don't, I won't bow. Make my obedience unconditional, not a deal I make with You.
07-09.text: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king. But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.
07-09.reflect: "Even if He does not." Is your obedience conditional?
07-09.act: Obey God in one area today regardless of the outcome.

07-10.prayer: God, guilty men run when no one's chasing them. Clean up my conscience so I can stand tall. Make me bold as a lion, because I've got nothing to hide.
07-10.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
07-10.reflect: Guilt makes men run. Righteousness makes men bold. Which describes you lately?
07-10.act: Clear your conscience on one thing so you can stand tall.

07-11.prayer: Jesus, Peter and John were ordinary men, but people could tell they'd been with You. Let people see that in me. Make my courage come from time with You, not from my resume.
07-11.text: When they saw the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they marveled and took note that these men had been with Jesus.
07-11.reflect: Their boldness came from time with Jesus, not education. How much time are you spending with Him?
07-11.act: Spend extra time with Jesus today before you face the world.

07-12.prayer: Lord, fear is going to show up today. When it does, I'll trust You. Not after I figure it out. Right then. Make that my first move, not my last resort.
07-12.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
07-12.reflect: David didn't say "if." He said "when." Fear will come. What will you do with it?
07-12.act: Memorize this verse. Use it the next time fear hits.

07-13.prayer: Jesus, call me out of the boat. I'd rather sink reaching for You than sit safe and never move. When I look at the waves, grab my hand and pull me back up.
07-13.text: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus. But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!” Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”
07-13.reflect: Peter sank, but he's the only one who walked on water. What boat are you hiding in?
07-13.act: Take one faith risk today. Keep your eyes on Jesus.

07-14.prayer: Lord, Caleb was still ready to take a mountain at 85. Keep me strong for the long haul, in body and in faith. Give me the courage to start the hard thing that builds that strength.
07-14.text: still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. As my strength was then, so it is now for war, for going out, and for coming in.
07-14.reflect: Caleb said this at 85. He was still ready to take a mountain. What will your body be ready for at 85?
07-14.act: Start a new physical challenge this month that scares you a little.

07-15.prayer: God, things are shaking around me. You're my refuge and strength, always present in trouble. Help me run to You first today, not last.
07-15.text: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song. God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas.
07-15.reflect: What's shaking in your life right now? Is God your refuge or your last resort?
07-15.act: Run to God first today when trouble hits.

07-16.prayer: Jesus, You never promised me an easy life. You promised trouble, and You promised You've already overcome it. I'll take courage in that today, and pass it on to a brother who needs it.
07-16.text: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!
07-16.reflect: Jesus promised trouble. He also promised victory. Which one are you focused on?
07-16.act: Encourage a man who's going through trouble right now.

07-17.prayer: Lord, Paul cared more about finishing his course than protecting his comfort. Help me finish my race. Show me the ministry You've given me, and keep me moving toward it.
07-17.text: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
07-17.reflect: Paul cared more about finishing than surviving. What's your course?
07-17.act: Do one thing today that moves your God-given mission forward.

07-18.prayer: God, Gideon was hiding when You called him a mighty man of valor. You see who I'll become, not just who I am. Call me forward, and give me courage to step into it.
07-18.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
07-18.reflect: Gideon was hiding when God called him mighty. God sees who you'll become, not just who you are.
07-18.act: Step into one thing God's calling you to, even if you feel unqualified.

07-19.prayer: Lord, I care too much about what people think. Help me fear You more than people. Free me from needing their approval so I can live for Yours.
07-19.text: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
07-19.reflect: Whose opinion controls you? Your boss? Your buddies? Your wife? God's should matter most.
07-19.act: Make one decision today based only on what God thinks.

07-20.prayer: God, courage isn't a feeling. It's showing up and doing the work. Give me courage to do the work today, scared or not. You won't leave me until it's done.
07-20.text: David also said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.”
07-20.reflect: "Do the work." Courage isn't a feeling. It's showing up and doing the work.
07-20.act: Show up and do the work today, scared or not.

07-21.prayer: Lord, steady my heart for whatever news comes. I've avoided some things because I'm afraid of the answer, including my own health. Make me a man who faces bad news with trust, not avoidance.
07-21.text: He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
07-21.reflect: Lots of men avoid the doctor because they're scared of what they'll hear. That's not courage. That's avoidance.
07-21.act: Schedule the screening or checkup you've been dodging.

07-22.prayer: God, my strength runs out by mid-afternoon. Yours never does. I'm strong in You, not in me. Remind me of that before every hard moment today.
07-22.text: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.
07-22.reflect: Your strength runs out. His doesn't. Where are you running on your own power?
07-22.act: Ask God for strength before every hard moment today.

07-23.prayer: Lord, You're on my side. What can man really do to me? Help me stand on my convictions today, even if I stand alone.
07-23.text: The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
07-23.reflect: Worst case, what can people actually do to you? Now compare that to Who's on your side.
07-23.act: Stand firm on one conviction today, even if it's unpopular.

07-24.prayer: God, let Christ be honored in my body. In how I work, train, serve, and treat people. Give me boldness to live so You get the credit, not me.
07-24.text: I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed, but will have complete boldness so that now as always Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.
07-24.reflect: Paul wanted Christ honored in his body. How does what you do with your body honor Him?
07-24.act: Use your body today for something that honors God: serve, work, train, help.

07-25.prayer: Lord, I've been fighting this one alone, and I'm losing. This battle is Yours, not mine. I'll do my part, but I'm handing You the outcome.
07-25.text: And he said, “Listen, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem! Listen, King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army, for the battle does not belong to you, but to God.”
07-25.reflect: What battle are you fighting alone that belongs to God?
07-25.act: Hand that battle to God in prayer. Then do your part and trust Him.

07-26.prayer: God, ten men saw giants. Caleb saw Your promise. Give me Caleb's faith. Let me speak faith when everyone around me is speaking fear.
07-26.text: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”
07-26.reflect: Ten men saw giants. Caleb saw God's promise. What do you see?
07-26.act: Speak faith instead of fear in a conversation today.

07-27.prayer: Lord, I talk about everything except You. Give me courage to share my faith, with gentleness and respect. Make me ready when someone asks about the hope in me.
07-27.text: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect.
07-27.reflect: Could you explain your faith in two minutes? Have you ever tried?
07-27.act: Write out your two-minute story of how God changed you.

07-28.prayer: God, some of my brothers have weak knees and anxious hearts, and they won't say it. Help me strengthen them. Give me the words and the invitation that gets them moving again.
07-28.text: Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees! Say to those with anxious hearts: “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.”
07-28.reflect: Some of your brothers are struggling with their health and too proud to say it. Who comes to mind?
07-28.act: Invite a buddy to work out or walk with you this week.

07-29.prayer: Father, You're for me. If that's true, nobody can stand against me. That's enough. Help me stop hesitating and do the thing I've been putting off.
07-29.text: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
07-29.reflect: If God is for you, what's stopping you?
07-29.act: Make the call, send the email, or have the talk you've been dreading.

07-30.prayer: Lord, my courage grows from my hope, and my hope is in You. Strengthen my heart today. Remind me what I'm trusting You for, and keep me holding on.
07-30.text: Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.
07-30.reflect: Courage grows from hope. What are you hoping in?
07-30.act: Write down three things you're trusting God for.

07-31.prayer: Jesus, courage isn't one big moment. It's a lifetime of small ones. Make me faithful to the end. Keep me from quitting halfway, and let me finish this race strong.
07-31.text: Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison to test you, and you will suffer tribulation for ten days. Be faithful even unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
07-31.reflect: Courage isn't one big moment. It's faithfulness every day until the end.
07-31.act: Recommit to finishing strong. Tell a brother so he can hold you to it.

08-01.prayer: Lord, I don't need more buddies who agree with me. Give me men who sharpen me, even when it throws sparks. And make me one who sharpens them.
08-01.text: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
08-01.reflect: Sharpening creates sparks and friction. Do you have friends who'll push back on you?
08-01.act: Ask a friend this week: "Where do you see me drifting?"

08-02.prayer: God, I know a lot of guys but have few real friends. Give me a friend who sticks closer than a brother. Show me who that might be, and help me invest in him.
08-02.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
08-02.reflect: Lots of buddies isn't the same as one real friend. Who's your one?
08-02.act: Call that one friend today. Not text. Call.

08-03.prayer: Lord, someone I know is carrying something heavy right now. Help me carry my brother's load. Don't let me just feel bad for him. Let me actually show up.
08-03.text: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
08-03.reflect: Who's carrying something heavy that you know about? What are you doing about it?
08-03.act: Help carry one man's burden this week. Show up, call, or bring a meal.

08-04.prayer: God, it's easy to let my men's group slide. Keep me showing up for my brothers. Make me the guy who spurs others on, not the one they have to chase down.
08-04.text: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds. Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
08-04.reflect: Skipping men's group becomes a habit fast. Are you showing up?
08-04.act: Commit to your group or find one. No excuses this month.

08-05.prayer: Lord, I tell You my sins but hide them from everyone else. Give me the guts to be honest with another man. Healing comes through confession, and I want to be healed.
08-05.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
08-05.reflect: Healing comes through confession to each other, not just to God. Who knows your real struggles?
08-05.act: Confess one struggle to a trusted brother this week.

08-06.prayer: God, Jonathan gave up a throne for his friend. Give me a Jonathan, and make me one. Kill the competition in me and help me want my brothers to win.
08-06.text: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.
08-06.reflect: Jonathan gave up his own shot at the throne for his friend. Are you that kind of friend?
08-06.act: Do something today that helps a friend win, even if it costs you.

08-07.prayer: Lord, even Moses needed men to hold his arms up. I'm not stronger than Moses. Give me brothers who'll hold me up when I'm tired, in my faith and in my health goals. Help me do the same for them.
08-07.text: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
08-07.reflect: Even Moses got tired. You'll quit your health goals alone. Who's holding your arms up?
08-07.act: Find a training partner or accountability buddy for your health this month.

08-08.prayer: God, flattery feels good, but it doesn't help. Give me friends who tell me the truth, even when it stings. And make me man enough to receive it and give it.
08-08.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
08-08.reflect: Do your friends only tell you what you want to hear? Do you?
08-08.act: Thank the friend who last told you something hard. Then tell a friend a hard truth with love.

08-09.prayer: Jesus, You laid down Your life for Your friends. Most days I won't even give up a Saturday. Teach me to lay down my life in the small ways, so I'd be ready for the big ones.
08-09.text: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
08-09.reflect: Most of us won't die for a friend. But will you give up a Saturday?
08-09.act: Give up something you want this week to show up for a friend.

08-10.prayer: Lord, anybody can be a friend when life is good. Make me a friend for the hard times. Bring to mind a brother who's struggling, and send me to him.
08-10.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
08-10.reflect: Easy to be a friend when things are good. Who's in a hard season right now?
08-10.act: Reach out to a man going through a divorce, job loss, or grief.

08-11.prayer: God, men rarely hear encouragement from other men. Use my words to build them up. Give me specific, honest things to say, and the courage to say them.
08-11.text: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
08-11.reflect: Men rarely hear encouragement from other men. You can change that.
08-11.act: Text three men today with specific encouragement.

08-12.prayer: Lord, when a brother falls, my first instinct is judgment or gossip. Help me restore him gently instead. And keep me watchful, because I'm not above falling either.
08-12.text: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
08-12.reflect: Restore, not shame. Gentleness, not gossip. How do you treat a brother who falls?
08-12.act: Reach out to a man who's fallen. Offer help, not judgment.

08-13.prayer: God, I become like the men I walk with. Help me choose my friends wisely. Lead me toward men who make me wiser, and give me the courage to step back from the ones who don't.
08-13.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
08-13.reflect: Look at the five men you spend the most time with. Are they making you wiser?
08-13.act: Spend more time this week with a man who makes you better.

08-14.prayer: Lord, my crew shapes how I eat, drink, train, and live. Surround me with men who build good habits. And make me the guy who raises the standard, not lowers it.
08-14.text: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
08-14.reflect: Your crew shapes how you eat, drink, and train. Are your friends pulling you toward health or away from it?
08-14.act: Plan one get-together this week built around something healthy: a hike, a game, a workout.

08-15.prayer: God, the early church devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, meals, and prayer. Devote me to real fellowship, not just small talk about sports and work.
08-15.text: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.
08-15.reflect: Teaching, fellowship, meals, prayer. Which is missing from your friendships?
08-15.act: Share a meal with a brother this week and pray together before you leave.

08-16.prayer: Lord, it's good and pleasant when brothers live in unity. Bring that to the men around me. If I'm at odds with a brother, give me the humility to go first.
08-16.text: A song of ascents. Of David. Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!
08-16.reflect: Is there a brother you're at odds with? What would it take to make peace?
08-16.act: Take the first step toward peace with a brother today.

08-17.prayer: God, four men tore off a roof to get their friend to Jesus. Make me that kind of friend. Show me who I need to carry to You, and give me the nerve to do it.
08-17.text: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men. Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
08-17.reflect: Jesus saw their faith. Four men carried their friend to Him. Who are you carrying to Jesus?
08-17.act: Invite a friend who doesn't know Jesus to church or your men's group.

08-18.prayer: Lord, help me feel what my brothers feel. Let me celebrate their wins without envy and sit in their losses without trying to fix them.
08-18.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
08-18.reflect: Can you celebrate a friend's win without envy? Can you sit in his loss without fixing it?
08-18.act: Celebrate a friend's win today. Out loud.

08-19.prayer: God, I'm tempted to talk about him instead of to him. Give me courage to handle conflict the right way: privately, directly, and with the goal of winning my brother back.
08-19.text: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
08-19.reflect: Do you talk to him or about him?
08-19.act: If you have an issue with a brother, go to him directly. Privately.

08-20.prayer: Lord, I spend a lot of time thinking about my own problems. Get my eyes off myself. Show me a brother's need today, and let me care about it like it's mine.
08-20.text: Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
08-20.reflect: When did you last ask a friend what he needs and then actually follow up?
08-20.act: Ask a brother how you can pray for him. Then pray all week.

08-21.prayer: God, I've gotten used to doing life alone, and it's costing me in my mind and my body. Heal the isolation. Give me the courage to reach out, and the humility to admit I need friends.
08-21.text: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.
08-21.reflect: Isolation is hard on a man's mind and body. Many men have no close friends. Is that you?
08-21.act: Make plans with a friend this week. Put it on the calendar.

08-22.prayer: Lord, David kept his promise to Jonathan long after Jonathan was gone. Make me loyal like that. Help me keep my word to my friends, even when it's inconvenient.
08-22.text: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
08-22.reflect: David kept his promise to Jonathan after Jonathan was gone. How loyal are you?
08-22.act: Keep a promise you made to a friend that you've let slide.

08-23.prayer: God, "let me know if you need anything" is easy to say and easy to forget. Help me love with action, not just words. Show me something useful to do for a brother today.
08-23.text: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.
08-23.reflect: "Let me know if you need anything" isn't help. Doing something is.
08-23.act: Don't offer help today. Just do something useful for a brother.

08-24.prayer: Lord, some friendships pull me closer to You, and some pull me away. Give me wisdom in my friendships, and the backbone to set boundaries where I need them.
08-24.text: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.
08-24.reflect: Is there a friendship pulling you away from God?
08-24.act: Set a boundary with one friendship that's dragging you down.

08-25.prayer: God, I can't flee temptation and pursue You on my own. Give me brothers who pursue You with me, men with pure hearts who call on Your name.
08-25.text: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
08-25.reflect: Flee and pursue, together. You can't do this alone. Who's running with you?
08-25.act: Ask a brother to pursue one spiritual goal with you this month.

08-26.prayer: Lord, Elisha refused to leave Elijah's side. Give me an older man to learn from, and give me a younger man to pour into. Don't let what You've taught me stop with me.
08-26.text: and Elijah said to Elisha, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to Bethel.” But Elisha replied, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
08-26.reflect: Elisha stuck with Elijah and learned everything. Who are you learning from? Who's learning from you?
08-26.act: Ask an older man you respect to meet with you. Or offer to meet with a younger one.

08-27.prayer: God, Barnabas vouched for Saul when everyone else was afraid of him. Make me a Barnabas. Show me who's been overlooked or doubted, and let me stand up for him.
08-27.text: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.
08-27.reflect: Everyone feared Saul. Barnabas vouched for him. Who needs someone to vouch for him?
08-27.act: Speak up for a man who's been overlooked or doubted.

08-28.prayer: Lord, sin hardens men slowly when no one's checking in. Help my brothers and me keep each other on track every day, in our faith and in our health.
08-28.text: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
08-28.reflect: Daily check-ins keep men from drifting, in faith and in health. Who checks in on you?
08-28.act: Start a daily check-in text with a brother: one workout, one prayer, one win.

08-29.prayer: God, let Your Word fill our friendships. Take our conversations deeper than scores and work. Let us teach, encourage, and even sing together with grateful hearts.
08-29.text: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
08-29.reflect: Do your conversations with friends ever go deeper than sports and work?
08-29.act: Share a Scripture verse with a friend today and tell him why it matters to you.

08-30.prayer: Lord, lots of men talk about loyalty. Few live it. Make me trustworthy. Let my friends count on me without having to wonder.
08-30.text: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
08-30.reflect: Talk is cheap. Can your friends actually count on you?
08-30.act: Follow through on every commitment you make today.

08-31.prayer: Jesus, You said the world would know we're Yours by how we love each other. Help me love my brothers like You love me: patiently, sacrificially, and without keeping score.
08-31.text: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.
08-31.reflect: The world knows you're His by how you love other believers. What does your love say?
08-31.act: Look back at August. Which friendship grew? Keep investing there.

09-01.prayer: Lord, my temptations aren't unique, and neither is Your faithfulness. You always provide a way out. Show it to me when temptation comes today, and give me the sense to take it.
09-01.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
09-01.reflect: There's always an exit. Are you looking for it or ignoring it?
09-01.act: Plan your exit for your most common temptation. Write it down.

09-02.prayer: God, sin starts as a thought, grows into a desire, and ends in death. Help me kill it while it's small. Catch my mind at the first thought, before it gets a foothold.
09-02.text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed. Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
09-02.reflect: Desire, then sin, then death. Where in that chain do you usually try to stop?
09-02.act: Stop it at the desire stage today. The first thought, not the third.

09-03.prayer: Lord, Joseph didn't stand there and negotiate. He ran. Give me the sense to run from what I keep trying to resist. Even if it costs me my coat or my pride.
09-03.text: She grabbed Joseph by his cloak and said, “Sleep with me!” But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.
09-03.reflect: Joseph didn't debate. He ran. What are you trying to resist that you should be running from?
09-03.act: Run from one tempting situation today. Physically leave.

09-04.prayer: God, I make a covenant with my eyes today. I'm deciding now, before the moment, where they will and won't go. Hold me to it, and remind me of it when I'm weak.
09-04.text: I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
09-04.reflect: Job decided ahead of time where his eyes would go. Have you?
09-04.act: Make your own covenant. Say it out loud to God.

09-05.prayer: Lord, You set the bar at my heart, not just my actions. Purify my thoughts. Show me what I need to cut off and what guardrails I need to put up today.
09-05.text: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
09-05.reflect: Jesus raised the bar to the heart. Where is your thought life taking you?
09-05.act: Install a filter or accountability software on your devices today.

09-06.prayer: God, David fell when he was idle and out of position. Keep me where I'm supposed to be. Fill my empty hours with purpose before the enemy fills them for me.
09-06.text: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing—a very beautiful woman.
09-06.reflect: David was supposed to be at war. Idle and restless, he fell. When are you most idle?
09-06.act: Fill your idle hours this week with something purposeful.

09-07.prayer: Lord, the enemy is prowling, and I make it easy when I'm tired, buzzed, or wired. Keep me clear-headed and alert. Help me take care of my body so I can stand guard over my soul.
09-07.text: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
09-07.reflect: Tired, buzzed, or wired men make bad decisions. Is anything dulling your mind?
09-07.act: Go to bed early tonight and skip the alcohol. Stay sharp.

09-08.prayer: God, purity doesn't come from willpower. It comes from guarding my life with Your Word. Keep me pure through it. Give me a hunger to read it, not just a sense of duty.
09-08.text: How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word.
09-08.reflect: Purity isn't willpower. It's guarded by the Word. How much Word is in you?
09-08.act: Read a full chapter of Scripture today.

09-09.prayer: Lord, plant Your Word deep in me, so it's there when I need it. I can't use what I don't remember. Help me hide Your Word in my heart this week.
09-09.text: I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You.
09-09.reflect: You can't use what you don't remember. How many verses do you know by heart?
09-09.act: Memorize one verse this week to fight your biggest temptation.

09-10.prayer: Jesus, You were starving in the desert and still said no. You fought with Scripture. Teach me to fight back the same way. Put the right verse in my mouth when temptation shows up.
09-10.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
09-10.reflect: Jesus was starving and still said no. He fought with Scripture. What do you fight with?
09-10.act: When temptation hits today, answer it with a verse out loud.

09-11.prayer: Jesus, You were tempted in every way I am, and You never caved. You understand. Thank You. I'm bringing You exactly what I'm struggling with, no hiding.
09-11.text: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.
09-11.reflect: Jesus gets it. He's not shocked by your temptation. Bring it to Him.
09-11.act: Tell Jesus exactly what you're tempted by. No hiding.

09-12.prayer: God, men with secrets never rest easy. Let me walk securely in integrity. If there's something I'd hate to have found out, give me the courage to bring it into the light.
09-12.text: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
09-12.reflect: Men with secrets never rest easy. Is there anything you'd hate to have found out?
09-12.act: Bring one secret into the light with a trusted brother.

09-13.prayer: Lord, nothing is hidden from You. My sin will find me out sooner or later. Help me confess it before it catches me, and give me grace when I do.
09-13.text: But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD—and be assured that your sin will find you out.
09-13.reflect: Hidden sin always surfaces. Better to confess it than be caught.
09-13.act: Deal with it before it deals with you.

09-14.prayer: God, I keep stocking the very things that trip me up. Help me cut off the supply line. Show me what to clear out of my house, my fridge, and my phone so failure isn't so easy.
09-14.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
09-14.reflect: "Make no provision" means don't stock it. Junk in the pantry, beer in the fridge, apps on the phone. What are you keeping within reach?
09-14.act: Remove one thing from your house or phone that makes it easy to fail.

09-15.prayer: Lord, guard what I put in front of my eyes. A lot of what I watch and scroll is worthless at best. Give me the discipline to delete it and the desire to fill that space with better.
09-15.text: I will set no worthless thing before my eyes. I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me.
09-15.reflect: What shows, sites, or feeds are worthless? Why are they still in front of you?
09-15.act: Unfollow, unsubscribe, or delete one worthless thing today.

09-16.prayer: God, integrity means being whole, the same man everywhere. Let my integrity guide me. Show me where I'm one man at church and another at work, home, or alone.
09-16.text: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.
09-16.reflect: Integrity means whole. Same man at church, at work, at home, and alone. Are you?
09-16.act: Pick the area where you're least consistent and fix one thing.

09-17.prayer: Lord, I want to dwell close to You. That means walking with integrity and speaking truth from my heart. Clean up anything in me that keeps me at a distance.
09-17.text: A Psalm of David. O LORD, who may abide in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy mountain? He who walks with integrity and practices righteousness, who speaks the truth from his heart.
09-17.reflect: Truth from the heart, not just the mouth. Do you believe what you say?
09-17.act: Be fully honest in every conversation today. No spin.

09-18.prayer: God, I tell more small lies than I want to admit. Exaggerations, excuses, spin. Strip the lies from my life. Make me a man who tells the truth even when it costs me.
09-18.text: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.
09-18.reflect: Little lies, exaggerations, excuses. They add up. Which ones do you tell most?
09-18.act: Catch yourself in one small lie today and correct it on the spot.

09-19.prayer: Lord, make my word good. Let my yes mean yes and my no mean no. Keep me from overcommitting, and help me follow through on everything I say today.
09-19.text: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.
09-19.reflect: If you need to swear on something for people to believe you, your word isn't good enough.
09-19.act: Only commit to what you'll actually do today.

09-20.prayer: God, I've been trying to resist the devil without submitting to You first. That's backwards. I submit to You now. Give me the strength to resist, and watch him run.
09-20.text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
09-20.reflect: Order matters. Submit first, then resist. Are you trying to resist without submitting?
09-20.act: Submit one area to God in prayer. Then resist temptation there all day.

09-21.prayer: Holy Spirit, I've used other things to take the edge off. Some of them have more control than I want to admit. Fill me instead. Be the One I turn to when the pressure's on.
09-21.text: Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to reckless indiscretion. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
09-21.reflect: What do you use to take the edge off? Is it controlling you more than you control it?
09-21.act: Take a break from alcohol this week. See what you learn about yourself.

09-22.prayer: Lord, I keep walking past the warning signs. Keep my feet off the wrong path. Show me the route, routine, or habit that leads me there, and help me change it today.
09-22.text: Do not set foot on the path of the wicked or walk in the way of evildoers. Avoid it; do not travel on it. Turn from it and pass on by.
09-22.reflect: Avoid, don't travel, turn, pass on. Four warnings. Where do you keep walking past the warning signs?
09-22.act: Change one route, routine, or habit that leads you toward sin.

09-23.prayer: God, Your will for me isn't a mystery here. You want me holy. Help me control my body in holiness and honor, and give me a brother I can be fully honest with.
09-23.text: For it is God’s will that you should be holy: You must abstain from sexual immorality; each of you must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor.
09-23.reflect: Wondering about God's will? This is part of it. Clear as day.
09-23.act: Tell an accountability partner where you stand in this area. Honestly.

09-24.prayer: Lord, test me. Examine my heart and mind. I'm a little afraid of what You'll find, but I'd rather know. Show me the blind spot I can't see on my own.
09-24.text: Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.
09-24.reflect: Do you want God to examine you, or are you afraid of what He'll find?
09-24.act: Ask God to show you one blind spot today. Pay attention.

09-25.prayer: God, I've told myself some things are harmless that could burn my life down. Keep me from playing with fire. Give me the wisdom to put real distance between me and it.
09-25.text: Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?
09-25.reflect: What "harmless" thing are you flirting with that could burn your life down?
09-25.act: Put distance between you and that fire today.

09-26.prayer: Lord, Your grace doesn't just forgive me. It trains me. Let it teach me to say no to ungodliness and yes to a self-controlled, upright life. Out of gratitude, not guilt.
09-26.text: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone. It instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age.
09-26.reflect: Grace doesn't just forgive. It trains you to say no. Are you letting it?
09-26.act: Say no to one worldly thing today because of grace, not guilt.

09-27.prayer: Search me, God. Know my heart and my anxious thoughts. This is a dangerous prayer, and I mean it. Point out anything offensive in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
09-27.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns. See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting.
09-27.reflect: This is a dangerous prayer. Are you willing to pray it and mean it?
09-27.act: Pray this slowly. Write down whatever God brings to mind.

09-28.prayer: Lord, a lot of things are allowed but not helpful. Sugar, caffeine, screens, nicotine. Don't let anything master me. Show me what I lean on too hard, and help me prove You're in charge.
09-28.text: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
09-28.reflect: Energy drinks, sugar, screens, nicotine. Not sinful by themselves, but could you go without? If not, who's in charge?
09-28.act: Pick one thing you lean on daily and go without it for three days.

09-29.prayer: God, Daniel's enemies dug through his work and found nothing. Make me blameless in my work. Clean up anything that wouldn't hold up to inspection.
09-29.text: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
09-29.reflect: Daniel's enemies dug and found nothing. What would they find on you?
09-29.act: Clean up one thing at work that wouldn't hold up to inspection.

09-30.prayer: Lord, I'm not strong enough to keep myself from stumbling. You are. Thank You for every temptation You helped me beat this month. I'm leaning on You for the next one.
09-30.text: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy.
09-30.reflect: You're not strong enough to keep yourself. He is.
09-30.act: Thank God for every temptation you beat this month. Lean on Him for the next one.

10-01.prayer: Lord, I treat prayer like a meeting I schedule and then forget. Teach me to talk to You all day long. In the truck, between jobs, during my workout. Keep the line open.
10-01.reflect: Prayer isn't a meeting you schedule. It's a line you keep open. Is yours open?
10-01.act: Pray short prayers all day: in the truck, between calls, during your workout.

10-02.prayer: Father, I'm shutting the door. No audience, no performance. It's just You and me. You see what happens in secret, and I want to meet You there.
10-02.text: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
10-02.reflect: Do you have a place where you meet God alone?
10-02.act: Pick your spot. Meet God there tomorrow morning.

10-03.prayer: Our Father in heaven, Your name is holy. Before I hand You my list, I want Your kingdom and Your will. Line up my wants with Yours today.
10-03.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
10-03.reflect: Jesus starts with God's name and God's will, not your wish list. How do your prayers start?
10-03.act: Start every prayer today with praise before asking for anything.

10-04.prayer: Father, give me what I need for today. Not a stockpile, just today. Forgive me the way I forgive others, and help me forgive like I actually mean that.
10-04.text: Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
10-04.reflect: Daily bread means daily dependence. And forgiveness flows both ways. Who haven't you forgiven?
10-04.act: Ask God for today's needs only. Then forgive one person.

10-05.prayer: Lord, lead me away from temptation today, before it finds me. Deliver me from the evil one. I'd rather ask for protection now than for forgiveness tonight.
10-05.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
10-05.reflect: Do you pray for protection before temptation shows up or only after you fall?
10-05.act: Pray this verse every morning this week before you check your phone.

10-06.prayer: God, I quit asking for some things because I got tired of waiting. I'm starting again. I'm asking. I'm seeking. I'm knocking. Give me the faith to keep at it.
10-06.text: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
10-06.reflect: What have you stopped asking God for because you gave up?
10-06.act: Start asking again. Write it down and pray it daily.

10-07.prayer: Lord, anxiety has settled into my chest, my jaw, and my sleep. I hand it to You with thanks for what You've already done. Guard my heart and mind with Your peace, the kind that doesn't make sense.
10-07.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
10-07.reflect: Anxiety shows up in your body: tight chest, clenched jaw, bad sleep. Prayer is God's answer for it.
10-07.act: When anxiety hits, stop, breathe slowly, and pray this verse. Then go for a walk.

10-08.prayer: God, You told me to call, and You promised to answer. I'm calling. Show me what I don't know, and give me the patience to sit quiet long enough to hear it.
10-08.text: Call to Me, and I will answer and show you great and unsearchable things you do not know.
10-08.reflect: Do you pray expecting God to answer? Or just out of habit?
10-08.act: Pray today, then sit in silence for five minutes and listen.

10-09.prayer: Lord, I've got a decision in front of me and I don't know the right call. I need wisdom. I'm asking, and You promised to give it generously. Make the way clear.
10-09.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
10-09.reflect: What decision are you facing that you haven't prayed about?
10-09.act: Pray about that decision before you make it. Ask a godly man for input too.

10-10.prayer: God, I've lost heart in prayer before. Some answers didn't come the way I wanted, or at all. Keep me praying when I want to quit. Don't let me give up on You.
10-10.text: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart.
10-10.reflect: Have you lost heart in prayer? What made you quit?
10-10.act: Pick back up one prayer you gave up on.

10-11.prayer: Lord, You hear me in the morning. I'm here before the noise starts. I'm laying my requests out in front of You, and I'm going to watch for Your answer today.
10-11.text: In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation.
10-11.reflect: David prayed and then waited with expectation. Do you wait, or just move on?
10-11.act: Pray first thing tomorrow before your feet hit the floor.

10-12.prayer: Holy Spirit, there are things I don't know how to pray about. Pray for me when I don't have the words. Take my groans and turn them into something the Father hears.
10-12.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
10-12.reflect: You don't need perfect words. Sometimes "help" is enough.
10-12.act: Bring God the thing you don't know how to pray about. Just sit with Him.

10-13.prayer: God, most of my prayers are about my will. Line them up with Yours. Teach me to pray for what I know You want: my family's faith, my purity, my growth.
10-13.text: And this is the confidence that we have before Him: If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.
10-13.reflect: Are your prayers mostly about your will or His?
10-13.act: Pray for one thing today you know is God's will: your family's faith, your purity, your growth.

10-14.prayer: Lord, I'm always moving, always on. Quiet me down. Slow my breathing, slow my mind, and help me be still long enough to remember that You are God and I am not.
10-14.text: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”
10-14.reflect: Men are always moving. Your body and mind need stillness to recover. When were you last truly still?
10-14.act: Sit still for ten minutes today. Slow breaths. No phone. Just God.

10-15.prayer: God, Nehemiah wept and prayed before he built. Break my heart for what breaks Yours. Show me what's broken around me that I've never brought to You.
10-15.text: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
10-15.reflect: Nehemiah prayed before he built. What's broken around you that you've never prayed about?
10-15.act: Pray about one broken thing in your community today.

10-16.prayer: Lord, Daniel prayed three times a day long before the lions showed up. Make prayer my habit, not my emergency plan. Build it into my day so it's there when the crisis hits.
10-16.text: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.
10-16.reflect: "Just as he had done before." Daniel's prayer life was set before the crisis hit. Is yours?
10-16.act: Set three prayer times today: morning, noon, and night.

10-17.prayer: Jesus, You were busier than I'll ever be, and You still pulled away to pray. Teach me to do the same. Help me find the quiet place and protect the time.
10-17.text: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
10-17.reflect: Jesus was busy and still pulled away often. What's your excuse?
10-17.act: Get alone with God for 20 minutes this week, outside if you can.

10-18.prayer: God, I complain about leaders more than I pray for them. Forgive me. I pray for our leaders today: my boss, my pastor, and those in authority. Give them wisdom, and give us peace.
10-18.text: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone— for kings and all those in authority—so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.
10-18.reflect: Do you complain about leaders more than you pray for them?
10-18.act: Pray for your boss, your pastor, and your local leaders by name today.

10-19.prayer: Lord, You promised to be there when two or three gather in Your name. Meet us when we pray together. Give me the nerve to pray out loud with another man.
10-19.text: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.
10-19.reflect: When did you last pray out loud with another man?
10-19.act: Pray with a brother this week. In person or on the phone.

10-20.prayer: God, I humble myself. I'm seeking Your face and turning from my own way. Forgive what I've done and heal what's broken, in me, my family, and my land.
10-20.text: and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
10-20.reflect: Humble, pray, seek, turn. Which one are you skipping?
10-20.act: Do all four today. Start with humility.

10-21.prayer: Lord, You are my healer. I bring You my body, with its aches, injuries, and the things I've been afraid to get checked. Give me humility to ask others to pray, and wisdom to see the doctor too.
10-21.text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
10-21.reflect: Pray and see the doctor. It's not either-or. Is there a health issue you've been too proud to pray about with others?
10-21.act: Ask your pastor or men's group to pray over a health need. Yours or someone else's.

10-22.prayer: God, I bottle things up. You told me to pour out my heart. So here it is, all of it. You're my refuge, and I trust You with what I've been holding in.
10-22.text: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah
10-22.reflect: Men bottle things up. God says pour it out. What have you been holding in?
10-22.act: Write a raw, honest prayer today. Hold nothing back.

10-23.prayer: Lord, Elijah was a man just like me, and his prayers moved heaven. Help me pray with that kind of persistence. Give me faith to pray big and keep praying.
10-23.text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years. Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.
10-23.reflect: Elijah was a man just like you. His prayers moved heaven. Why not yours?
10-23.act: Pray earnestly for one big thing today. Then keep praying.

10-24.prayer: I believe, Lord. Help my unbelief. My faith is real, but it's mixed with doubt. Like that desperate father, I'm bringing You both and asking You to work anyway.
10-24.text: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”
10-24.reflect: A desperate dad prayed an honest prayer, and Jesus answered. Is your faith mixed with doubt? Say so.
10-24.act: Pray this verse over the thing you struggle to trust God with.

10-25.prayer: Jesus, the night before the cross, You prayed for me. Thank You. Let that change how I see prayer, and make me a man who prays for others who don't even know it.
10-25.text: I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message, that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
10-25.reflect: Before the cross, Jesus prayed for you by name. Does that change how you see prayer?
10-25.act: Pray for someone today who doesn't know you're praying for them.

10-26.prayer: God, I'm in distress, and I'm crying out to You. You've heard me before, and You're hearing me now. Reach down and help me.
10-26.text: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for His help reached His ears.
10-26.reflect: Your cry reaches His ears. Every time. What's your distress right now?
10-26.act: Cry out to God about it. Out loud if you can.

10-27.prayer: Lord, I don't want prayer to be an afterthought. Devote me to it. Make me watchful for what You're doing and thankful for what You've done.
10-27.text: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful.
10-27.reflect: Devoted means committed, not casual. Is prayer a devotion or an afterthought?
10-27.act: Spend half your prayer time today just thanking God.

10-28.prayer: Lord, Isaac went out to the field to meditate. Meet me on the trail, the sidewalk, or the back road today. Let my body move and my heart pray.
10-28.text: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.
10-28.reflect: Isaac walked and prayed. Moving your body and praying go together better than you think.
10-28.act: Take a prayer walk today. Pray for every house or person you pass.

10-29.prayer: Holy Spirit, prayer is how I fight. Keep me alert in it. Help me pray for my brothers with every kind of prayer, and don't let me grow lazy in the battle.
10-29.text: Pray in the Spirit at all times, with every kind of prayer and petition. To this end, stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers for all the saints.
10-29.reflect: This verse comes right after the armor of God. Prayer is how you fight.
10-29.act: Make a prayer list of five men. Pray for them every day this week.

10-30.prayer: Lord, the disciples watched You pray and wanted what You had. Teach me to pray. And let my kids and the younger men around me want what they see in me.
10-30.text: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
10-30.reflect: The disciples watched Jesus pray and wanted what He had. Who's watching you pray?
10-30.act: Let your kids or a younger man hear you pray today.

10-31.prayer: God, let my prayers rise to You like incense, my hands lifted like an offering. Thank You for meeting me this month. Help me keep the habits You've built.
10-31.text: May my prayer be set before You like incense, my uplifted hands like the evening offering.
10-31.reflect: Your prayers are an offering to God. How has your prayer life changed this month?
10-31.act: Set one prayer habit from this month that you'll keep for good.

11-01.prayer: Lord, I'm quick to notice what's missing and slow to notice what's here. Train my heart to give thanks in everything. Not for every hard thing, but in it, because You're still in it.
11-01.text: Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
11-01.reflect: In every circumstance, not for every circumstance. What hard thing can you still give thanks in?
11-01.act: Write down five things you're thankful for. Do it every day this month.

11-02.prayer: God, Paul had to learn contentment, and so do I. Teach me. Whether I have plenty or not enough, let my peace come from You, not my circumstances.
11-02.text: I am not saying this out of need, for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances. I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. I am accustomed to any and every situation—to being filled and being hungry, to having plenty and having need.
11-02.reflect: Paul learned contentment. It didn't come naturally. Are you learning it or fighting it?
11-02.act: Go one day without wishing for something you don't have.

11-03.prayer: Christ, You are my strength in every season. Not just to win, but to be content when I lose. Give me strength for this season, whatever it holds.
11-03.text: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
11-03.reflect: This verse is about contentment, not touchdowns. Christ gives strength to be content in plenty and in need.
11-03.act: Thank God for His strength in your current season, whatever it is.

11-04.prayer: Lord, I came into this world with nothing, and I'll leave with nothing. Godliness with contentment is the real gain. Make that my goal, and loosen my grip on the rest.
11-04.text: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it. But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.
11-04.reflect: You came with nothing. You'll leave with nothing. What are you chasing in between?
11-04.act: Give away something you don't need this week.

11-05.prayer: God, free me from the love of money. It promises security, but You're the only One who never leaves. Help me be content with what I have because I have You.
11-05.text: Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said: “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”
11-05.reflect: Contentment comes from God's presence, not your bank account. Which are you leaning on?
11-05.act: Skip one unnecessary purchase this week. Thank God instead.

11-06.prayer: Lord, I usually come to You with complaints and requests. Today I come in with thanks. Before I ask for anything, I want to bless Your name for who You are.
11-06.text: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.
11-06.reflect: Thanksgiving is the way in. Do you start prayer with complaints or thanks?
11-06.act: Start every prayer today with thanks only. Ask for nothing until you've thanked.

11-07.prayer: Lord, You forgive my sin and You heal. I won't forget what You've done for my body and soul. Thank You for every breath, every step, and every day I can still train and work.
11-07.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds— He who forgives all your iniquities and heals all your diseases.
11-07.reflect: Can you walk, lift, breathe, and see? Most men only thank God for their health after they lose it.
11-07.act: Thank God for five things your body can do. Then use one of them today.

11-08.prayer: Jesus, ten were healed and only one came back. I've been one of the nine more than I'd like to admit. Make me the one who comes back to say thanks.
11-08.text: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice. He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
11-08.reflect: Ten were healed. One came back. Which one are you?
11-08.act: Go back and thank God for a prayer He answered that you never thanked Him for.

11-09.prayer: God, I keep thinking the next raise or purchase will settle me. It never does. Show me that more won't satisfy me. Only You will.
11-09.text: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
11-09.reflect: What number would be "enough"? Be honest. Did you hit it before and want more?
11-09.act: Thank God today for what you earn. Don't think about the next raise.

11-10.prayer: Lord, my life isn't measured by my stuff. Guard me from greed in every form. Show me what possession has too much of my heart, and help me let go.
11-10.text: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
11-10.reflect: Your life isn't your stuff. What possession has too much of your heart?
11-10.act: Loosen your grip on one possession. Lend it, share it, or give it.

11-11.prayer: God, You made today, and I'll rejoice in it. Thank You for the men and women who paid for my freedom. Help me spend this day in a way that honors their sacrifice.
11-11.text: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
11-11.reflect: Today's a gift. Veterans paid for many of our days. How will you use this one?
11-11.act: Thank a veteran today. Then make today count.

11-12.prayer: Father, every good thing in my life came from You: my wife, my kids, my work, my health. Forgive me for treating gifts like they're owed to me. Open my eyes to them today.
11-12.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
11-12.reflect: Your wife, your kids, your job, your health. All gifts. Do you treat them that way?
11-12.act: Tell God and one person about a gift you've been taking for granted.

11-13.prayer: Lord, kill the comparison in me. I keep measuring my life against another man's truck, house, and paycheck. Help me bless him instead of envy him.
11-13.text: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
11-13.reflect: His truck, his house, his paycheck, his life. What do you covet most?
11-13.act: Pray a blessing over the man you envy. Mean it.

11-14.prayer: God, social media is full of other men's highlight reels. Help me stop comparing my body and progress to theirs. Let me run my own race and thank You for how far You've brought me.
11-14.text: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
11-14.reflect: Social media is full of other men's highlight reels: bodies, lifts, race times. Comparison will steal your joy and your consistency.
11-14.act: Compare yourself only to where you were last year. Write down how you've grown.

11-15.prayer: Lord, my lines have fallen in pleasant places, better than I deserve. Help me see the life You've given me with grateful eyes instead of restless ones.
11-15.text: The lines of my boundary have fallen in pleasant places; surely my inheritance is delightful.
11-15.reflect: Look at the boundaries of your life. Where has God been better to you than you deserve?
11-15.act: Walk your property, your neighborhood, or your workplace and thank God for it.

11-16.prayer: God, even if the business fails, the money dries up, and the crops don't come in, I'll still rejoice in You. Make my joy rest on who You are, not what I have.
11-16.text: Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls, yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
11-16.reflect: Could you still praise God if the business failed? If the money dried up?
11-16.act: Praise God today for who He is, not for what He's given.

11-17.prayer: Lord, the people around me hear me complain more than they hear me give thanks. Change that today. Keep praise on my lips and catch me every time I start to grumble.
11-17.text: Of David, when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, so that the king drove him away. I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise will always be on my lips.
11-17.reflect: Do the people around you hear you complain or give thanks more?
11-17.act: No complaining today. Every time you catch one, replace it with a thank-you.

11-18.prayer: God, I'd rather have little with You than a lot without You. If chasing more is bringing turmoil into my home, show me, and give me the courage to choose peace.
11-18.text: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
11-18.reflect: Is your pursuit of more creating turmoil at home?
11-18.act: Choose peace over profit on one decision this week.

11-19.prayer: Lord, moths and rust will get everything I own eventually. Help me invest in what lasts. Let my calendar and my checkbook show that my treasure is in heaven.
11-19.text: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal. But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
11-19.reflect: Where are you storing your treasure? Your calendar and your bank statement will tell you.
11-19.act: Invest time or money in something eternal this week.

11-20.prayer: God, You're good, and Your love never quits, no matter what this year has held. Thank You. Help me tell my family where I've seen Your goodness.
11-20.text: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.
11-20.reflect: God's goodness doesn't depend on your circumstances. Do you believe that today?
11-20.act: Tell your family one way God has been good to your house this year.

11-21.prayer: Lord, thank You for the food on my table and the people around it. As the holidays come, help me eat with gratitude, enjoy what You've given, and bless You when I'm satisfied.
11-21.text: When you eat and are satisfied, you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.
11-21.reflect: Thanksgiving week is coming. Food is a gift to enjoy with gratitude. Eat until satisfied, then thank the Giver.
11-21.act: At every meal this week, pause and give thanks before and after. Then go for a walk with your family.

11-22.prayer: God, let Your peace rule my heart, not my stress or my grudges. Show me where I need to make peace before the holidays, and make me thankful while I do it.
11-22.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
11-22.reflect: Peace and thankfulness travel together. Where are you missing both?
11-22.act: Make peace with one person before Thanksgiving.

11-23.prayer: Lord, You love a cheerful giver, and I can be a reluctant one. Make me generous and glad about it. Show me someone in need I can bless this week.
11-23.text: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
11-23.reflect: Do you give grudgingly or gladly?
11-23.act: Give generously to someone in need this week. Smile while you do it.

11-24.prayer: God, I'll give thanks with my whole heart and tell what You've done. Give me the words at the table this week, and the courage to say them.
